utterances.text: But in substantial terms, though he stayed in Central Bosnia for another month or so, did you succeed in taking over the military police even though he was appointed to a higher position?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, because I was accorded the right to control and command the 4th Military Police Battalion or the 7th Military Police Battalion and to have control over the commander of the military police, whereas Pasko was responsible for the Light Assault Battalion of the military police which was a combat unit of the military police over which I had no jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: This new Light Assault Battalion, was it developed from the former Jokers?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and also as a result of an attempt to form a Light Assault Brigade attached to the military police as we had mentioned before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned the term "4th Military Police Battalion or the 7th Military Police Battalion." What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is the same unit, only for one period of time it was called the 4th Military Police Battalion and later on, with the reorganisation, it came to be called the 7th Military Police Battalion, but it is actually the same military police battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us read another part of this text on page 12 of the Croatian original of the book "Three Years of the Military Police," published in 1995, and in the English version, it is page 17, third paragraph. I shall read it: (as read) "To unify military police activities and duties and those of light assault battalions and battalions of the military police in the respective Operative Zones, the Assistant Chiefs of military police administrations are charged, those who were appointed for each Operative Zone. The same persons are also authorised to command those battalions through the commanders of those battalions." And a few rows further down, it says: "The Assistant Chief for the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia ... Mr. Pasko Ljubicic." This text from 1995, is it in conformity with what you knew and what you have just told the Court?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It says here that, in order to unify military police activities and tasks of the light assault battalions and the military police battalions in the respective Operative Zones, the Assistant Chiefs of military police administrations have been assigned these duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please, 523. Defence Exhibit 523.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Nobilo. May I ask you, General, this question: I am trying to put together the various pieces of evidence to which we have listened and to compose some kind of a macro picture of the situation. Now, I gather from the text which we just saw that there were a few Operative Zones in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, for a time there were four Operative Zones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Four. This may have been said already. In a sense I am only retracing the steps. So there were four Operative Zones, and the military police, was operating in each of those four zones?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: And they were answerable to a central command situate where?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, you mean of the military police?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: They were accountable to the military police administration which was based in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mostar.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: And for a time also in Ljubusko, but I don't know the exact dates, from when until when it was in Mostar and from when until when in Ljubusko. For a time it was also in Posusje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So the Central Bosnia Operative Zone was one of the four Operative Zones?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, what was the relationship between the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and the Lasva Valley; were they one and the same thing?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was not the same area because the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia included also a part of the area under HVO control in Kiseljak, Zepce, and, for a time, also a part of the area of Sarajevo that was under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So the Lasva Valley was smaller in area than the Central Operative Zone of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Don't bother. I'm only trying to perfect my macro appreciation of the situation. Now, would I be correct in supposing that, in each of the Operative Zones, each of the four Operative Zones, there was a military contest going on at one level or another between the HVO and the BiH?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I apologise, but I had some difficulty with understanding, but I do understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Are you sure? Would you wish me to try again? I'll try again.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Was it the situation that, in each of the four Operative Zones, there was a military contest going on at some level or the other between the HVO and the BiH?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps there may have been but not on the same scale. In the Operative Zone of Bosanska Posavina in the north of Bosnia, as far as I know, there were no conflicts between members of the HVO and members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. There, the units were joint. They acted jointly in the HVO, that is, both Bosniak Muslims and Croats of Bosanska Posavina were in the HVO, but eight municipalities of Bosanska Posavina, seven to eight municipalities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Then in what Operative Zones would you say that a military contest was going on between the HVO and the BiH?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the Operative Zones of southeastern Herzegovina with the command in Mostar and which had competence over the southeastern Herzegovina; then in the Operative Zone of northwestern Herzegovina with the command post in Tomislavgrad; and in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: As we mentioned the Lasva Valley and the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, tell Their Honours, from the 16th of April, 1993 onwards, which part of the Operative Zone did you, in fact, control?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had control over the Lasva pocket, which means this part here that is surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you show us on the map, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can show you on the map. It is this area here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Which municipalities are they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Twenty per cent of the municipality of Novi Travnik, about 10 per cent of the municipality of Travnik, about 35 per cent of the municipality of Vitez, and about 40 per cent of the municipality of Busovaca. That is the area here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you enumerate the municipalities that formally belonged to the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia but over which you were not able to have any effective command or any command, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Those were the municipalities of Kiseljak, Kresevo, Fojnica, Kakanj, Vares, Stup Sarajevo, a part of Hrasnica, Zepce, Maglaj, a part of Teslic, Usora.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Would it be helpful if the witness would demonstrate very briefly on the map what size of area he's talking about, so that one could then make a comparison between the pocket as described and the other area which he thinks really constituted the Central Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may be of assistance, there is an exhibit in the Prosecution Exhibits early on, and I can pull it, where we have put that into evidence. The Central Bosnia Operative Zone is delineated on a map municipality by municipality. I don't think it's a subject of contention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Very good, Mr. Kehoe. Would it be convenient at this particular stage if the witness would briefly demonstrate with his pointer on the map what is the other area that is being talked about?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps on the map below if it is bigger.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it's bigger. I would be very willing to show you, Your Honours, but we don't seem to have a map here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the other map?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. It's more or less the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to follow from the other map. The one on the easel is convenient for me, but I understand your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Judge Shahabuddeen, it's Exhibits 27 and 28, Prosecution Exhibits. I think the witness testified there were minor variations in the Operative Zone, so the appropriate exhibit is Exhibit 28.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Number 27 or 28?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's 28 for this time frame, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What year was that, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There was a change in the Operative Zone in October of 1992, so what we have in Exhibit 28 is October of 1992 onward through 1993, 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I wouldn't proceed with it, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your Honours, the exhibit that my learned colleague mentioned is on the ELMO, and the green letters denote the municipalities of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. The witness can now indicate what he controlled in 1993, mid 1993, and what was not under his control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you please point out what you controlled in mid 1993?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In mid 1993, I was located in the area from the Travnik municipality, Nova Bila, 10 per cent of the area there; from the Novi Travnik municipality, 20 per cent of the area; of the Vitez municipality, 35 per cent of the area; and Busovaca, about 40 per cent of the area. That is what we call the Lasva pocket (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, please, who was around you, around that Lasva pocket?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had the forces of the BH army, the 3rd Corps, the 6th Corps, and parts of the 1st Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Around the pocket, was it a continuous front?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, and this can be clearly seen here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One last question. There's a large area in green on the map which is on the ELMO. If you look at the ELMO -- are you looking at the ELMO? There is a large area in green. Is that whole area of the Central Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Part of the area, Your Honours, are but the municipality of Teslic, the complete -- that area was not in the Central Bosnia area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Could you point to Teslic, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Teslic is here (indicating), the municipality of Teslic. Just a small portion of the Teslic municipality leaning on the Zepce municipality, in the borderline region, was within the composition of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, but the complete municipality of Teslic never was. Then we have the municipality of Tesanj. That was not within the composition of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone but only a part of the Usora municipality which is part of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Can you help me this way, General? I know it's difficult, but I'm trying to compose a macro view of the situation. Can you indicate what fraction of the whole of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone was represented by the pocket as it has been drawn on the map there? You were enclosed within a pocket. Well, now that pocket constituted a quarter, a half, three-quarters, or what portion of the total area? Can you do it that way?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can show you, Your Honour, but I don't know how much it is of the overall area of Central Bosnia. I can show you and tell you in relation to the municipality --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: As roughly as you can, can you say that it was about a half or about a quarter? We wouldn't hold you down minutely.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this is the smallest area of the remaining part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. A similar pocket to this existed in Kiseljak, and we called it Operative Group 2, and a similar pocket to this pocket was in Zepce as well, and we called that Operative Group 3, and an even smaller pocket existed in Usora, but we considered that it was with Operative Group 3, under Operative Group 3. If you look at it in relation to the Kiseljak and Zepce areas, then that is the smallest area surface-wise of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Do I understand you this way: Then the HVO controlled other pockets within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, other than, shall we say, the Vitez-Busovaca pocket?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. There were three other pockets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I need a clarification. If I've understood correctly, there was a disparity between the opinions of the Defence and the accused in respect of the boundaries of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Mr. Kehoe, is that so? Because a little while ago when we looked at the map, I thought that I understood that this was a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It is a Prosecution document, and I'll tell you how this was put together. During an interview with the accused some time ago, the questioner asked the witness what localities, what municipalities were part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Now, in fairness to both the questioner and the witness, whether or not they actually had a map to delineate where Teslic or Tesanj -- the Central Bosnia Operative Zone cut off or not, I'm not certain. Nevertheless, this particular exhibit is based on that discussion, and to the extent that there are imperfections in this exhibit vis-a-vis Teslic and Tesanj, we stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me. General Blaskic, on the map which is on the ELMO, Visoko does not appear to be in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, but I think that Visoko was included, was it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, you are right, that is to say, Visoko was not in the composition of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. It was not in the composition of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, even the Zavidovici area and Maglaj. There were certain HVO units in Zavidovici and Maglaj, but practically the whole time, they were together, or at least up until the 24th of June, 1993. There was a joint command in existence for the defence of Maglaj, so the BH army and the HVO together, but the HVO never supervised the whole of Maglaj and Zavidovici, just as it did not for the whole of Teslic and Tesanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But I do think that, during these discussions, we have to clarify the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. There must be a document. When you took command in the fall of 1992, there must have been a document from your superiors which would delineate your zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I only had a blue notebook, a wartime diary, that is to say, but there was no precisely drawn-out map. I can return and enumerate the municipalities which entered into the Central Bosnia Operative Zone when I took over my duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, I hope that you had a clear idea. There is enough confusion already in respect of which units you commanded. We would like to know on the territory or on the ground, what it was that you commanded. When you took over the command, when you went through command, through village or, I think they were called, brigade commands -- I think it was a Defence or Prosecution Exhibit; I don't remember -- but I seem to remember that all the municipalities were well indicated. In any case, you knew what it was that you commanded, at least I hope so.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is correct. As far as I know, without my notebook, I can say that on the 25th of November, 1992, a document on the establishment of the HVO brigades, that exists. But as far as I know and recall, I spoke at the beginning about that, I can enumerate the municipalities of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone for you now, if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, could you just tell us whether today you recognised map as being valid, that is, theoretically, that is, valid in respect of covering your theoretical command of the Operative Zone. Then I do understand, I assume that in respect of the military situation and the war with the Bosnian army, I do understand that the zone was formed, and then other enclaves were added to it, that there would be enclaves. But theoretically, did you make any comments about the map? According to the Prosecution, in some way, you approved the map, or approved of the map which is on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is a Prosecution Exhibit, the map that is on the ELMO. We would like to suggest that we place a translucent foil over these municipalities so that the witness can draw in by hand what was formerly within the composition of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Perhaps that would help us most. So to place this foil over the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: My colleague is speaking about the operations using the map that he has in front of him, but I do understand that your command zone evolved. But for General Petkovic -- if today General Petkovic were here, would he recognise that that was the Operative Zone which he had given to you, theoretically? I can see Mr. Hayman is not pleased with this, and therefore, there must be a discrepancy in respect of the delineation of the zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps that is why it would be best for the witness to draw in the boundaries. Perhaps he knows best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is a document in the record -- excuse me, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: There is a document in the record that Mr. Harmon is looking for now, and I do believe it is a Defence document concerning the reformation of the brigades as they formulated in November of 1993 where these particular municipalities are delineated. This, of course, was prior to the conflict in January of 1993. Prior to that time, municipalities such as Gornji Vakuf, et cetera, were part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone. They then were taken out of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone as of October of 1992 and made part of the Northwestern Herzegovina Operative Zone under the command of Colonel Siljeg. We then had the particular municipalities that are set forth in this exhibit which were then part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone. To the extent the witness says that there were areas that were not part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone in Teslic and Tesanj, that is not reflected in the exhibit, the document that's in evidence to date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What worries me is the word "operational material." I think we have to be -- unless, of course, in the archives, with transparencies, I am afraid that if we just clip things, they will get lost, because the transparency is valid only if it is really attached properly to the map. Otherwise, the usher is going to be put in as an exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, would you please explain the symbols? You have an uninterrupted line and a dotted line. Would you explain what it's about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this dotted line on the map encompasses the municipalities of Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Jablanica, and Konjic. Those are the municipalities which, at the beginning, that is to say, 1992, when I took over my duties, that is June and July, were within the composition of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Sometime in October 1992, these municipalities were conjoined to the Operative Zone of Northwest Herzegovina with headquarters in Duvno, or Tomislavgrad, rather. The other parts of the map, with this full uninterrupted line, is the Central Bosnia Operative Zone in that it was never agreed -- the authority over this, it was never agreed between the 3rd Corps and the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, the 3rd Corps of the Bosnian army, because the areas are superimposed. There are two armies, two authorities, they overlap, and the 3rd Corps kept authority over Bugojno and Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But, General, when General Petkovic, in the defence department in Mostar, at the point where the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was set up, when that General gave you a command, he was not concerned with the 3rd Army Corps. He gave you a command, a territory. Here's where I think the ambiguity lies. In other words, my question -- well, I can tell you it is a very simple question -- perhaps it is also complicated. When General Petkovic or the minister of defence at Mostar, when the entity was constituted, that entity which was called the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, when he gave you command of the Operative Zone in Central Bosnia, was Teslic part of that? I think it's simple.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, part of the Teslic municipality was. That is, we're talking until the 12th of August, 1992, when this territory was lost. The Serbs had conquered it I think somewhere between the 8th and 12th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, did you want to clarify something? Then I think we're going to stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Maybe we're talking at cross-purposes here. The bottom line is Teslic, for instance, was part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone just like Jajce was part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone, and the fact of the matter is, as combat activities with the Bosnian Serbs progressed, part of Teslic was lost, part of, of course, Jajce was lost, but they still remained part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone. That issue never changed. Now, when and where the line at different times changed is a separate issue, but it was still part of the Central Bosnian Operative Zone and still part of what was declared as the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Thank you, Mr. Kehoe. I think that this is a difficult discussion because I believe that you, who are a leader in a war, a military commander in the midst of a war, you see this territory moving, depending upon battles that were either won or lost. I have to say that today what I'm interested in is to whether there was an agreement, of course with you, among the leaders, that is, an agreement in order to define the frontiers of the Operative Zone which was given to you as your responsibility. Then, of course, if you lose territory, of course, I understand it is no longer there, and, of course, I understand as well that the operative map is going to change. But when you were given the Operative Zone in Central Bosnia, and I think that you answered my question, but at that point, Teslic was not a part of it.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, a part, a small part -- I cannot tell you accurately what percentage -- but I can say that it wasn't even 10 per cent. I think that it is called the Komusina parish, in other words, a village, a parish, which is bordering the Zepce municipality made part -- so that part of the Teslic municipality did make a part of the Operative Zone. In other words, that small part. But I never had an opportunity to enter Teslic because a brigade of the Bosnian Serb army was there, and the Teslic municipality was always under the control of the Bosnian Serb army, and when I was in Jajce, I spent over a month and a half working on the defence of the town of Jajce. Now, that is a completely different situation. In Jajce, I was there together with the BH army, and the BH army and we have controlled most parts of the Jajce municipality, then lost it to the Serbs, but with respect of the Teslic municipality, we didn't even control 10 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. I think it's clear. During the cross-examination, the Prosecution can ask the questions that it wants. Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, General, one last question: You were in the Lasva Valley pocket.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The HVO controlled two or three other pockets within the Central Bosnia Operational Zone; is that correct? Kiseljak was one and I think you mentioned two others.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, let me try to be specific here. The HVO controlled additional four pockets, that is, in addition to the Lasva Valley pocket. One of them was Kiseljak, the second was the village of Dastansko in Vares municipality, the third was Zepce, and the fourth was Usora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: What I am trying to be clear about in my own mind is this: Were you in command of these other HVO pockets within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On paper, I indeed was the commander of those surviving four pockets, which I basically did not even enter until the Washington Accords except when I was taken to Kiseljak in U.N. vehicles for meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I appreciate your help. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to suggest that the witness mark with a red marker the Busovaca-Vitez area where he was able to move, that is, on the transparency, if you would show in red, if you can shade the area to which you had physical access, in other words, where you could move around physically?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. So now we are seeing what the Operative Zone looked like and what the pocket within that Operative Zone looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, just by way of qualification? I mean, this exhibit, of course, is talking post November of 1992, and I think counsel will agree that the witness is talking post April 1993 with regard to this red marker there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. This is why I suggest that the witness write down the date as of which the Lasva Valley looked like this, and perhaps mark the eastern border of Bosnia and Herzegovina so that we can then offer it and enter it as a separate exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just the eastern border, and this is how we will be able to always put it on top of a map of Bosnia and Herzegovina and find our proper bearings there.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, if you will just write in the date as of which this enclave, that is, mark in red, existed, where you would move around without encountering a BH army presence. So you can just mark it on the transparency itself.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May I now ask the registrar to mark this for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is D540 -- pardon me, D550.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you. It can be removed now, and now if I can have the witness please be shown D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can counsel repeat the number of the exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It would be enough to simply put a line on the right side in order to find the match there. I think that Judge Rodrigues would prefer to have a line on the left side. I don't see any problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. If we can just adjust it so that it covers it completely? In black marker, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Please, Exhibit D523.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I find this so very helpful, that may I suggest that we leave it on the ELMO, or wherever, until we return? I may ask the witness to be so good as to indicate some of the other positions which he mentioned on the transparency, but I won't do that now. It is a matter for the Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Shahabuddeen, I agree with you. I suggest that we now take a 15-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President? Just excuse me, Counsel, before we begin. Judge Shahabuddeen, before the break, I did refer to an exhibit wherein the accused had delineated the various municipalities in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. That is Defence Exhibit 200.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did you say "Defence Exhibit" or "Prosecution Exhibit"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's Defence Exhibit 200 put in through Brigadier Marin. In that document, it is dated the 7th of October, 1992, there is a reformation of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone discussing the various municipalities that are now in the zone, as well as those in the various groups within the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. I knew there was an exhibit in there some place, Judge, and I, with the assistance of Mr. Harmon, just found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Now we have to give it a number, that is, the transparency itself is a Defence Exhibit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: All right. We took a transparency that was superimposed on a Prosecution Exhibit, and in the meantime, we made a colour copy of the transparency superimposed on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Which could be given a number then. So we have to give a number to the colour photocopy that was just made; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. This would be the Defence Exhibit number D550, and now I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're 45 exhibits behind, Madam Interpreter. It's 550.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I would like to suggest that we introduce the transparency as 550 and the complete picture which comprises both the transparency and the underlying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. That's just as clear as the transparency itself. All right. I think we all understand what we're talking about now. It is the transparency which will be given the number 550, and all of us in our files will have the copy which will have the same number. We can now continue. Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I hope I'm not making matters too difficult, but I wanted, pursuant to an earlier indication, to invite the witness to indicate on the same transparency some other positions to which he had, indeed, referred. In the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, you said that there were three other HVO pockets; Kiseljak was one, and I think there were two others. Would it be possible for you to indicate on the transparency where those other HVO pockets were?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you like me to draw it in or just point?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I would prefer to see you draw it in. Maybe there are other colours of pens.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Could you go over that again to give it some more brightness?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: That's the Kiseljak area, I imagine?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour. This is the Kiseljak area (indicating). The next one is the area of Vares (indicating).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes. So there are five pockets.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One last thing. You said that there were four Operative Zones; the Central Bosnia Operative Zone was one of the four Operative Zones. Is it possible for you to indicate on the map where the other three were?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can show it. I can both draw them in or show them, point to them. The municipality of Orasje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I don't know if you have another coloured pen which can be used. If you can indicate it with a pen, I will be very grateful. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It got set off a little bit. Can you just readjust it? Let's try to make it as accurate as possible, please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It's not cooperating with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. This is the registry pen. The other pens were the Defence pens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I don't know of the exact connotation to be affixed to those remarks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have to make the date clear, Judge Shahabuddeen. Please ask them to specify a date because we put down a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge is quite right. There's a date which you have indicated. Would you indicate the positions with reference to this date, "April 1993"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we have to go back to the Defence marker.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is correct. The dates are different, but I can also write them down on the transparency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: No. The President is quite right. There is a date on the map, "April 1993." Would it be possible for you to keep that date in mind and, as of that date, to indicate where were the other Operative Zones?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, using this marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It got set off again, so if you can just put it back.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Marks). This is the area of the Bosanska Posavina Operative Zone, headquartered in Orasje, and it covers predominantly the Orasje municipality (indicating). This is the northeastern Herzegovina Operative Zone with its command post in Tomislavgrad, and the command post was in Prozor (indicating). I don't know the exact dates when it was in Prozor and when it was in Tomislavgrad. This is the southeastern Herzegovina Operative Zone with the command post in Mostar (indicating). For awhile, it was also in Citluk, that is, the command post of the command of the southeastern Herzegovina Operative Zone. Again, I do not know the exact dates as to when it was in Citluk and when it was in Mostar. Then I do not have enough transparency for the Orasje Operative Zone and for the Neum Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One last point, General. Can you indicate on the map the position from which overall command was exercised over all these four Operative Zones?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, you mean the command post of the HVO main staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For a while, the main staff was in Mostar and then in Citluk, but it had its forward command posts in Prozor and, for a period of time, in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, I would like to follow on from what Judge Shahabuddeen has said and ask you: Can we say, when the HVO lost control over certain municipalities such as Gornji Vakuf, Konjic, Jablanica, and so on, or at least the period of the year, what time of year it was, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you this, as regards the period of the year. In 1993, somewhere up until the 20th of April, 1993, the HVO lost control over Konjic and Jablanica, I think; that is to say, up to the 20th of April, 1993, I'm certain, but I think it was until the 15th of April, 1993, so Konjic and Jablanica. In Gornji Vakuf, this already took place in January 1993, that is to say, January, when there was a positioning of forces of the BH army and the HVO, so that in the later period, part of the town was under the control of the BH army and the other part of the town was under the control of the forces of the HVO. I know today the exact boundaries, but I didn't know at that time who held what. But, for the most part, the road from Gornji Vakuf up to Novi Travnik, that is, this road here (indicating), Your Honours, this road was completely under the control of the BH army forces of the 308th Brigade from Novi Travnik and the Mountain Brigade from the composition of the 3rd Corps from Gornji Vakuf. I'm not sure of the number of that particular brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mentioned Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bugojno fell, that is to say, it was taken over by the BH army, on the 26th of July, 1993. Bugojno, here we have it (indicating), and Kiseljak was brought into this situation between the 16th and 17th of July, 1993. Vares and the expulsion from Vares occurred between the 3rd and 4th of November, 1993, and Zepce from the 24th of June, 1993. In the next 15 to 20 days, it was brought into a position of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you show us the border of the Republic of Croatia and the two Herzegovina Operative Zones on the map?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. In the area of the Livno and Duvno and Posusje municipalities, that is the Operative Zone of Northwest Herzegovina, and then we have Grude, Ljubuski, Capljina, and Neum, that is the Operative Zone of Southeast Herzegovina, and that is the border with the Republic of Croatia, that's the frontier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, I have a question which won't take very long to answer. When the General speaks about losses, I believe that most of the losses were among the Serbs; is that correct? We already know that Bugojno was lost for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Let me ask the question a different way: During the fighting between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, did the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina lose territories to the Serbs and, if so, what were those losses?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am trying to think, because it relates to the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not Central Bosnia, and I was in the pocket then, but perhaps I can use the knowledge that I have today and tell you exactly because during the fighting, the Serbs took over the territory, in my opinion, and that is my personal opinion, it was the territory that was necessary for them to take over for the purposes of their strategy, that is to say, Eastern Bosnia, directly along the border of the River Drina, that is to say, Srbrenica and the other regions, Zepa, part of Gorazde, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General, when you say "during the fighting," you're talking about the fighting between the HVO and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood the question. That means during the conflict between the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the HVO, what the Serbs took over during that time, they expanded their corridor of Posavina to the north, they expanded the corridor, and they took over the region along the eastern borders, that is to say, Srbrenica, Zepa, Konjevic Polje, Cerska, so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, you said what the Serbs had taken control of, but tell the Trial Chamber now, please, the municipalities that you mentioned and said that they were the Operative Zone of southeastern Herzegovina which was lost, but who took control of those municipalities?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Central Bosnia, all the municipalities were taken over by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and placed them under its control, and as there was a withdrawal of HVO forces in one of two ways that I described earlier on, then the Croats withdrew together with the HVO to the remaining territories under HVO control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, if we forget about the area of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and if we were to look at the territory of Northwest Herzegovina, Konjic, Jablanica, Gornji Vakuf, Bugojno, who took control of that region?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That was taken control of by the BH army and the forces of the 4th Corps of the BH army, to be precise, parts of the 6th Corps of the BH army, parts of the 1st Corps and 3rd Corps of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: In this entire region which does not lean upon the Republic of Croatia, border with the Republic of Croatia, did the HVO have an expansion of territory under its control anywhere?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it did not because the overall municipality of Bugojno, from the 26th of July, was taken over by the BH army, and most of the Croats there left the area, and about half and perhaps more of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf, as well as the whole of the municipality of Konjic and, according to our intelligence data, in Jablanica, at the end of 1993 and the beginning of 1994, there were only 14 families left, 14 households left living in Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: You mean Croatian?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Croatian. So that area was taken over by the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about the territory that was compactly leaning and bordering on Croatia; did the HVO lose anything there or did it hold its positions or did it win over any territory, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This territory bordering on Croatia, that is to say, the municipalities of Livno, Duvno, Posusje, Ljubuski, Capljina, Neum, and part of the municipality of Stolac, for the most part, were retained in the same composition; they were not taken over, for the most part, by the BH army. But there was fighting, there were battles in that area as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: May we move on to document D523?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. I'm sorry. We're not getting a translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the microphone wasn't switched on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you can ask it again?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. I will repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, you have before you a Defence Exhibit, it is D523, and it represents part of the rules and regulations of the military police from 1994, the beginning of 1994. In Article 10, points 1 to 10 enumerate all the tasks of the military police. Would you take a look at them, please? We're not going to read them all so we don't lose much time, and tell the Trial Chamber, please, whether the military police tasks and jobs were the ones stipulated here when you took over. That's the first question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Now, could you delineate for the Court, by looking at the ten principal tasks of the military police, which tasks are daily operative police tasks and which tasks are the military use of the military police, point by point? Which points are the military use and which were the daily military police tasks; could you differentiate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All the points except, with the exception of point 9, are, for the most part, daily tasks, and with the exception of point 8. Point 9, "Taking part in accomplishing military tasks at the front line under the order of the minister for defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: That is a combat task, is it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What about point 8? Point 8, is it a combat task or is it a daily operative task?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, point 8 talks about "taking part in fighting terrorist, rebellion and other enemy formations," and taking part in fighting tasks come under the orders of the defence minister, so that point 8 could be a combat task, although it is not expressly stated in Article 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If it is not expressly stated that it comes under the command of the minister of defence, from those positions, what status would point 8 have?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, point 8 would be a daily operative task then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did this kind of division exist in 1993, according to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let us go back to August 1993 and you appointed Palavra as commander. Tell us what happened next in the days that followed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Nobilo. General Blaskic, when the military police were given to you for what they call daily tasks, when was that? Starting from the 16th of April, do you remember, 11.42, for example -- were you always told that the military police had been sent to you for daily tasks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For daily military police tasks, that is to say, daily tasks, this was in January 1993, sometime in January '93, for daily tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Under point 10, it says that you needed a special authorisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Point 9, Your Honour. Point 9, Your Honour, of Article 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, point 9 under Article 10. It says that you needed special authorisation from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There was to have been attachment of the military police for me to have the right to utilise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What I would like to know is -- I would like you to talk about point 8. That's what I'm interested in. Here's my question: If the military police went to Ahmici on the 16th of April in the morning, between 5.30 in the morning and 11.42, in your opinion, it went into Ahmici -- if it went in -- under what point, according to this Article? I suppose it must have been covered by point 8.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, point 9, point 9. It could only take part in the fighting according to point 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Therefore, the police went, in your opinion, if it went, it went to Ahmici based on point 9 between 5.30 and 11.42 whereas it was not attached to you; that's what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The military police were attached to me from the moment when the commander of the military police reported to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But when you were not contacted by the military police commander, did the military police -- did it depend on you or was it subordinate to you for daily tasks? Was it subordinate to you for daily tasks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For daily tasks, yes, but not for combat tasks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Let me go back to my question now: Could one conceive that between 5.50 or 5.30, rather, in the morning, and 11.42, the military police was acting in Ahmici on the 16th of April under point 8, and at that point, the military police was attached to you, that is, it was taking part in fighting terrorist, rebellion, and other enemy formations. I'm asking you: Could one consider that the military police penetrated into Ahmici between 5.30 in the morning and 11.42 acting on daily tasks covered by point 8 but for which you would be responsible? What feeling do you have about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think we can because we're talking about the combat use of forces of the military police, and the military police, for it to be used in combat operations, had to have an order issued by the defence department. That is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I understood that. That's point 9. Now you're repeating point 9 to me. I understood that for a military operation, a combat military operation, the military police could not act with you and under your orders unless it had authorisation from the ministry of defence. But what I am interested in is point 8, and the question that I was asking you is to know whether, for the daily tasks, the military police was attached to you? That's my first question. Was the military police attached to you for daily tasks, "Yes" or "No"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the military police, but not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you yourself are telling me that all the points that are in this Article 10 are points which indicate daily tasks except for point 9. So let's take 9 by itself. Point 9 says that you are responsible for the military police starting from 11.42. Do we agree on that? That's how I understood you. Now, I was asking whether one could consider that the military police acted within the scope of point 8 which, in your opinion, is a point which involves daily tasks.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is why I said that in point 8 -- point 8 talks about taking part in fighting and it lists against whom, so if you imply and if you assume the use of the military police, then we go to point 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, you see, but this is where you're not being clear enough, General Blaskic. Do you acknowledge that it is only point 9 which provides for an order from the ministry of defence, only point 9 that provides for the order from the ministry of defence?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, as far as I recall -- perhaps I was not clear enough -- but point 8 says, and I quote, "Taking part in fighting," which means that the use of the military police is permitted, and this is why I said, when counsel asked me, that point 8 could also be made part of point 9 because it implies the use in combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you acknowledge that you're adding things to the text because that's not in the text. It isn't in the text.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am only offering you an opinion. It is true, it is not in the text, but it says in the text "Taking part in combat." Mr. President, with your permission, if what was meant was fighting the anti-terrorist groups, I don't know what the legislator had in mind there. Perhaps it would be clearer. But if you mean the military police, as it says here, the whole Article says the use of the military police; in other words, if you were talking about the tasks of the military police. My understanding of it is that it implies taking part in combat by the military police in fighting, and for that, you need permission of or an order of the minister of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether you're right or whether you're wrong, General Blaskic. Nonetheless, in respect of command structures, once, under point 8, it has not been provided that a specific order from the Ministry of Defence attaches a police to you, one could assume and suggest, one could assume that the military police went to Ahmici thinking that it would be fighting rebels, terrorists, and other enemy formations, considering that it was under your command, daily tasks, that is. I assume that you don't agree. I'm quite sure that you don't agree. I'm sure that you don't agree, but I'm using your reasoning when I allow myself to say to you that you are the one who is interpreting "taking part in fighting" as meaning, under point 9, under the order of the Ministry of Defence, and I say that you are adding things to the text. We can't go any further than that. I simply wanted to take the liberty of raising this question with you. I won't say anything further. I'm not drawing any conclusions from that, but it is starting from your logic that I allowed myself to ask that question. I think we can continue. Judge Shahabuddeen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: May I, General, pursue just a little the inquiries opened up by the President? Between 5.30 in the morning of the 16th of April and, I think, 11.42, the military police were subordinate to you for purposes of military duties not involving combat operations; is that the position, as you saw it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The military police had been attached to me for the daily police tasks, which do not include combat activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, is it correct to say that the military police were attached to you by an order, as it were, for ordinary military duties or was that the general rule under a document which you discussed with us last week? For ordinary military duties, was there any necessity for an attachment order to be made?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: For the usual or ordinary police duties, no order of attachment was necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: All right. Now, you later saw what was done at Ahmici. What was your view, that what was done was done in the course of ordinary military duties or was it your view that what was done was done in the course of combat duties?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that this was a combat task, that is, combat activity. But from whom this task was issued, I cannot say, but in any event, it was not regular police activity like patrols, control of persons, or such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge, was any order issued by anyone authorising the military police to engage in such combat duties?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not know by whom the military police may have received such an order. I believe that the military police commander should have received an order, and I assume that he had received an order on attachment. I do not know from whom he received such an order for combat operations, but my impression is that it was an organised and systematic activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: You also considered that what was done amounted to serious crimes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did you check your assumption that the commander of the military police would have received an order authorising him to engage in such combat duties?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I checked all the reports which I had received, and later on, I launched an investigation after I had learned of what had taken place in Ahmici. I did not check the military police commander because the commander never reported in his reports on what had taken place. I considered this to have been done behind my back and that he must have had some knowledge of this, but he never informed me of it in any way, shape, or form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did you ever discover the existence of any order from anyone authorising the commander of the military police to engage in combat duties between 5.30 in the morning and 11.42 in the morning of the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I later on received information from the security service that the investigation in the territory of Central Bosnia had been completed and that the file, including the list of the suspects, had been sent to the security administration in Mostar, but I was not in a position to ever open that file and familiarise myself with its contents regarding the investigation of the crime in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: So as you sit there testifying to the Trial Chamber today, you cannot say that you discovered any order authorising the commander of the military police to engage in the combat duties which led to the commission of the crimes at Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Personally, I did not see such an order. Whether the commander received it or not, Your Honour, I do not know this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: One last question. Assuming that the military police are answerable to you for daily tasks and assuming that they engage in combat duties without any order from any superior authority, would you say that that was an act of insubordination to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I may not have fully understood your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I'll put it again. Let it be assumed that the military police are answerable to you for daily tasks. Let it also be assumed that they engage in combat duties without any order from any superior authority authorising them to engage in combat duties. Would you have taken the position that the military police, in engaging in such combat duties in such circumstances, were guilty of an act of insubordination to you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In any event, this would have been the self-will of the military police, but I was not authorised to issue them combat tasks without the proper foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I know that and I wouldn't pursue it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: So if you cannot issue combat tasks and the military police acts without an order of their superior officer, to whom are they insubordinate to at the time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: To the one who is competent to issue orders to them, in other words, to the command and to the chief of the defence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you have any information that any terrorist group or something like that had been in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had no information of any terrorist groups in Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you consider the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is, its 3rd Corps as a terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, was there a front line developed through the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please look at point 9: "Taking part in accomplishing military tasks at the front line." What happened on the 16th of April, if we can for a moment set aside the crime, how can we define what took place in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: If we think of the front line, then it is the taking part in accomplishing military tasks at the front line, point 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Can you now describe for us point 8? A typical situation from life which would be covered by point 8; in other words, what was behind this taking part in the fighting of the sabotage terrorist groups?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: We had such a situation when there was an incursion of a group in the village of Jardol. Early in the morning, around 5.00 a.m., a group of Mujahedin entered the village of Jardol, opened fire and started killing everything in sight. Special forces, special intervention forces, are used to break up such groups, but it only takes place when a terrorist group had been discovered and its area of operation had been identified, and then both the military and the police forces come in and fight them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: If you look at your enclave, we know that you had a front line all around your enclave. Would the catching of a terrorist group be a task of the units which are defending the outside line of defence of the enclave or of the units which are working in the depth of the territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: According to any doctrine, both in the JNA and in Bosnia, it was a task of the civilian police and the military police and the civilian authorities, that is, in the depth of the territory. Sometimes it is defined as combat control of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The sabotage terrorist groups, are they inserted into the front lines or into the depth of the territory?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, they are always inserted behind the front lines, that is, into the depth of the territory, and usually they are the best equipped and best trained members of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let's disregard all the points here, but tell the Trial Chamber, did you send the military police to the village of Ahmici to accomplish any task?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Did you order them to commit the crime in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, you have answered many questions already. Let's take a 10-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We can resume now. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence wanted to note for the record that there is a translation problem with the English translation of Defence Exhibit 523. This was a version we had translated, I think, the night before we used it the first time by a staff member in Mr. Nobilo's office in Zagreb. Your Honour, Mr. President, noted problems in the translation on the 19th of January of this year at transcript page 17216 and asked that a professional translation be done by the Registrar's office. We haven't gotten that back yet, and we would ask that that be done. One of the issues, Mr. President, is that I believe that the proper translation is not going to be -- in point 8, it's not going to be "formations" but "groups," suggesting smaller, perhaps internal groups of persons, as opposed to formations on the front line posing an external threat to the territory under consideration. We apologise that we weren't able to provide, back when we first used the document, a professional translation, but we would reiterate your prior request that a professional translation be made. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. This is an important point for our discussions, and it would be good for the registrar to be sure that a perfectly correct translation be made of that point specifically. Please continue, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: General, after you installed Marinko Palavra as the commander of the military police, and before you go on to further activities of the military police, from the 10th of August 1993 onwards, tell us about the activities included.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, on the 10th of August, 1993, I asked the assistant for security to continue the investigation with regard to the crime in Ahmici because the results of the investigation thus far, I was not satisfied with. I considered that all the changes in the military police would create a far more favourable climate for the assistant for security to implement a complete investigation as to the crime in Ahmici. In addition to that, on the 10th of August, I received information on the killed soldiers in the Lasva pocket, that is to say, the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, in fact, and there were a total of 1.293 soldiers that were killed; injured, 3.750 soldiers, so about 5.043 soldiers who were incapacitated on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When you say "soldiers," do you mean HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I mean HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From 16.10 to about 18.00 or 18.40, I had a meeting with the representative of the UNHCR, Mr. de la Mota. He came to me and he complained that the military police had made it impossible for him, from Stari Vitez, to evacuate to Zenica two Bosniak Muslim families. I told him on the occasion that this evacuation was contrary to his mandate of the UNHCR and any movement of the population was ethnic cleansing, and I told him that in that case, he himself was working against his own mandate. Mr. de la Mota told me that this was an exception and that it was necessary to transport the family to Zenica so as to be able to link it up with the other family members who were already in Zenica. We discussed the issue once again, that is to say, the problem of freedom of movement and the issue of ethnic cleansing and contrary stands of the International Red Cross and the UNHCR. On the 11th of August, 1993, I had a meeting with the European Monitors, that is to say, with Mr. Watkins, who tried to inform me of the events in Bugojno, and he requested of me information about the events in Zepce and Kiseljak, he asked me to tell him of those events, and I told him that Bugojno was not in my zone of responsibility and that the situation in Zepce and Kiseljak for me was something I did not know, I didn't know about that, because I was receiving only superficial information which reached me after a considerable lapse of time. Mr. Watkins, at that meeting, told me that the Croats of Central Bosnia were the greatest casualties in the aggression. On the 12th of August, 1993, I was informed in the late afternoon that a meeting had been held in a private cafe, privately-owned cafe, at Mr. Drago Kajic's place, between 15.00 until 18.00, and the participants in that meeting were the head of the centre for security on behalf of the Muslim Bosniak police forces, this was Mr. Asim Fazlic from Zenica and together with him was also Mr. Ivan Nedoklan, and on the other side, we had representatives of local armed groups or bands, Mr. Andric, Zuti, nicknamed "Zuti," and Mr. Dzandara and Mr. Boro Lovrinovic. This meeting was organised through the mediation of a liaison officer of the UNPROFOR command in Nova Bila, and the topic of the meeting was the possibility of giving over the explosives factory and the Lasva pocket, rendering it to the BH army along with monetary remuneration for that, recompense, and a price was even discussed, the price to be offered for the local armed groups to take control of the factory and forcibly take over command in the Lasva pocket and to surrender, to turn over the factory in the Lasva pocket to the 3rd Corps of the BH army. Later on, in the days that followed, I told Colonel Duncan that I knew of the meeting, I intimated to him that I knew that the meeting had taken place and that this was below the level of officers to enter into organising meetings of that kind between various local groups and the head of the security service of Zenica. On the 14th of August --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. May we hear Duncan's reactions?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that moment, he just looked down. He didn't deny that the meeting had taken place. The officer, liaison officer, from his battalion introduced himself as Mr. Perry, he was a captain by rank, and he mediated in transport from Zenica to the cafe, the officers from the 3rd Corps and the Bosniak Muslim representatives from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Would you remind us, please, one of the representatives -- you say in a very nice way "the members of an armed group," but I would like to say Mafioso groups -- you mentioned Zuti. Is it the same Zuti that witnesses from the International Community mentioned who was responsible for the hijacking of convoys?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it was. He was one of the bosses in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: When we're discussing this matter, tell us, please, in the days that followed, were candidates put forward for command of the Operative Zone, and if the answer is "Yes," then tell us, in 1993, who was one of your competitors? Tell the Court that.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, candidates began to make themselves known at the end of May 1993, and I received information later on about a talk between Zuti and Darko Kraljevic, that they would take over command of the Operative Zone, and Zuti was even offered a certain post in the command of the Operative Zone, and Darko would have been the commander, Zuti would probably have been the deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: What do you think, with hindsight and at this point in time, had you been able to tender your resignation, had that been possible in those war days, would it have been realistic to say that Darko Kraljevic and Zuti would have taken over the Operative Zone or the pocket in which you moved?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am absolutely certain that that would have happened, that the command would have been taken over by one of those two men. I believe that it would have been Darko Kraljevic, I am inclined to believe that it would have been Darko Kraljevic, because he was more powerful, he had a strong unit, and he had the type of status and he was a local man and he was deputy head of the security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 14th of August, 1993, a general offensive was launched by the BH army on Vitez and there was exceptionally heavy fighting from the morning up until 21.00. In the course of that entire day, we had civilian casualties from Grbavica from the BH army and their snipers caused this. On the 16th of August, 1993, I once again insisted, with the assistant for security, that a complete investigation into Ahmici be continued, and I was also engaged, in the course of the day, in ensuring free passage for the UNHCR convoy and the International Red Cross towards Kruscica and Stari Vitez, and I had talks with the representatives of the International Red Cross about mediation to receive a permit for the evacuation of the wounded from the Nova Bila hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Before you continue, may we have document D379 because it is dated the 17th of August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Therefore, we have document D379. It is your own order dated the 17th of August, 1993, and you issued the order to the commander of the Josip Ban Jelacic Brigade in Kiseljak. The title is "Demolition of a religious object (a place of worship)." "Today, the 17th of August, 1993, we have been informed of a demolition of" as it says "a religious object in Kiseljak, (a place of worship). "In order to establish the facts and conduct investigation, I hereby order: 1. You are to send in a detailed report about the demolition of this place of worship. 2. You are to inform me what you have done in respect of conducting an investigation and finding the perpetrators. 3. You are to inform me what facts you have established and what action you plan to undertake regarding this incident." Typed in three copies. TB/SV. Tell us, please, is that your own order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this is my order. I wrote it. This can be seen by the initials at the bottom, TB, Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Tell us, what does it mean when you order the commander of the brigade which is formerly -- command to say that you have been informed on the 17th of August that a demolition took place of a place of worship? Should he not have informed you of that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, this means that I received information from another source and not from a report sent by the commander because, as I have already said, communications were sporadic and very brief, and that is why I ask him, under number 1, to "send in a detailed report" as to the circumstances of the demolition of this place of worship. I do not know which place of worship it was in the Kiseljak municipality and I don't know whether it was intentionally demolished or whether the demolition took place in the course of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Point 2, you ask him to conduct an investigation and to identify the perpetrators. Can we draw any conclusions as to the information you received, how this facility was demolished?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I received information that the place of worship that was demolished was a mosque, and I therefore asked for an investigation to be conducted and to find out who the perpetrators were because this conduct was contrary to my order on the protection of places of worship, including mosques, and we talked about this earlier on when we looked at other exhibits, so other places of worship as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the next order, another order on investigation into Ahmici. I think it is so important that perhaps we should not start discussing it at the end of the day but to leave it for tomorrow morning perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, Mr. Nobilo. All right. We will resume tomorrow, tomorrow's Thursday, and we will resume at 10.00. Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of March, 1999, at 10.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
